design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (d3, stock-rotation return behind the anniversary review due today) — revision 2

[Why a good test] The caller asks for one thing: a stock-rotation return of leftover BR-31406 bearings after an ordinary return was declined. The scored RMA quantity (28) is the product of a 6-factor allowance computed over 12 months of ship-to shipments, a StockSmart ledger (d4), the credit ledger (d1) and the contract (d2), and it is only correct on the world in which today's anniversary review has moved the plant from Corbett Route Delivery Ship-To to Corbett Priority Ship-To — a review whose own result is a 4-factor computation over route usage, tenure-based measure selection and drop-ship/will-call shares. Difficulty comes from reading the rotation rule, discovering its wait sentence, seeing in the ship-to record that the anniversary is today and unreviewed, and getting two computations right; tools judge nothing.

[Scope] Claimed: order_ext_anniversary_review (prereq, record_anniversary_review_a2ef3cef, agent) and order_ext_stock_rotation_return (root, submit_stock_rotation_return_550cd403, user). Task 1 holds reactivation and the requested move up. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[4,6]: the review takes 4, the rotation 6.

[Problem-tree card] root order_ext_stock_rotation_return; edge -> order_ext_anniversary_review, kind value_input, gate rotation_rate_pct, form action, sentence: "The stock-rotation allowance is fixed only after the review of the ship-to's service level for its most recent opening anniversary has been recorded." Four-point test: connective 'only after'; XX is a plainly named business action (the review being recorded); no tool/id/code token; hard requirement for the most recent anniversary only. fallback_reason: the review leaves variant_name and last_review_date, which the customer-elected level change also writes, so no record state singles out the review. Derivation: sentence + ship-to record (opened 2019-10-14 -> anniversary 2026-10-14 = today; last_review_date 2025-10-14) + the review rule ('the review falls due on the anniversary ... the review date is the day the review is recorded') -> the anniversary review, measured on the twelve months ending today. Unresolved at frozen_time: initial_state.ship_to_accounts.86fcf081-....last_review_date = 2025-10-14 < 2026-10-14. Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skipping the review gives 40 instead of 28 (rate 10 instead of 7). Order review -> rotation; single edge.

[Factor card — review (4)] review_route_use_pct (parameter, multi-source: route level AND route_truck count): 4 runs < 6 -> 85% (baseline 70% keeps Route). review_tenure_basis (method, selection rule): open 84 months (>= 60) -> lower of counted twelve-month 54194.00 and twice counted six-month 50080.00 (baseline counted twelve-month 54194.00 keeps Route). review_dropship_share (parameter): 7.04% -> 50% (baseline: 51917.50, keeps Route). review_willcall_share (parameter): 19.36% -> 50% (baseline: 55358.00, keeps Route). All-baseline keeps Route. Near-misses: route shipments 2025-06-10 and 2024-12-03 outside 12 months; the 2025-10-22 route shipment just inside (11 whole months); the 2026-04-14 credit exactly 6 whole months back, outside the six-month figure.
Method pairwise table (review_tenure_basis): (a) MN(C12, 2*C6), (b) MX(C12, 2*C6), (c) C12; C12 = 100, C6 = 30 -> 60 / 100 / 100; C6 = 70 -> 100 / 140 / 100 — every pair differs on some input; (a) and (b) are opposite selections, (c) a single figure.

[Factor card — rotation (6)] rotation_rate (parameter, multi-source: level AND months open): Priority & 84 months -> 7% (baseline 5% -> 19). rotation_base_scope (method, cross pricing): Category Contract -> bearings 36268.75 (baseline all merchandise 62804.25 -> 40). rotation_standing (parameter, cross credit): active + returned payment 2026-05-19 -> 50% (baseline 100% -> 40). rotation_program_share (parameter, cross vmi): active program -> 20000.00 added (baseline 0 -> 17). rotation_unit_value (parameter, cross pricing_items; it selects the divisor): repriced 61.60 effective 2026-06-01 after the 2025-11-20 shipment, only line of that date on CPA-31206 -> divide by 61.60 (baseline 64.80 -> 27). rotation_cap (parameter, cross pricing): commitment 75000 -> cap 4000 (baseline 1500 -> 24). All-baseline -> 23. Near-misses: the defective RMA-305936 credit (369.00) is not a customer reason; the 2025-09-22 StockSmart bill is outside 12 months.
Method pairwise tables: rotation_base_scope (a) category 12m, (b) sku 24m, (c) all 12m — on this world 36268.75 / 6966.00 / 62804.25. (rotation_unit_value is a parameter since revision 3: its tiers select the divisor — the later lower contract price, the invoiced price less the aged-stock markdown, or the invoiced price; the rotation keeps one method factor, rotation_base_scope.)

[Base-invariant card] Review write (order_service_level_changed): order_ship_to_lifecycle and order_agg_ship_to_portfolio carry no eligibility gate on it (policy_scope); the base downgrade half-sentence is retired by overwrite for the anniversary review only. RMA write (order_return_authorized): order_evt_returns gates inside_return_window (retired for stock-rotation returns only; replaced_by restates the window for every other customer-reason return) and returnable_quantity (inherited: 28 <= 60 shipped - 0 open). The base exclusions (non-returnable classes, special orders, opened items) are inherited in the rotation scope sentence and tested on the records (stock_status, item_class) and on the customer's statement (unopened).

[Business-object card] Target line SO-3104417 line 2 (BR-31406), one shipment 60 @ 64.8000 on 2025-11-20; key (order_number, line_number) from the declined request RMA-307215 — the only order_return_declined line on the ship-to (alone on its date). Excluded: SO-3104417 line 1 (BR-31390), sister ship-to ST-31907, prior RMAs on other lines.

user_scenario:
You are Renata Malloy, the purchasing and storeroom lead at Kinsman Extrusion, Inc. in Cleveland. You are brisk, organised and a little tired of chasing paperwork; you talk like someone who has a count sheet in front of her. Earlier this year the company shut down Line 3 at the Euclid Avenue plant, and the maintenance crib there is sitting on a shelf of pillow block bearings, Corbett item BR-31406, that nobody will use now. Two weeks ago you asked Corbett to take 40 of them back and the request was turned down because it was past the return window. A colleague at another plant told you Corbett has a stock-rotation return for slow-moving stock, and that is why you are calling today: you want to send back as many of those 40 bearings from the Euclid Avenue plant as Corbett will take under a stock rotation. You are fine with a partial number if that is all the program allows; you are not asking for any other credit, refund or price adjustment.

You open by saying who you are, which company, and that you want to set up a stock-rotation return for the leftover bearings at the Euclid Avenue plant after your earlier return was declined. You give the account number C-318452 when the agent asks for the account, and if the agent needs a second detail to confirm who you are you give the main phone number on the account, 2164531870. If the agent asks about the condition of the bearings, you say all 40 are still sealed in their original boxes, never opened. If you are asked which order the bearings came on, you say you believe it was the November order for the plant and that the declined return should be on file; if asked for the declined request's number you read it from your email: RMA-307215. You do not know the account's service level, review dates, contract terms or how any allowance is figured, and you say so plainly if asked.

If the agent explains that something has to be updated or recorded on Corbett's side for the plant before the rotation can be worked out, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead. Once the agent tells you how many bearings can go back, you accept that number without arguing. If the agent offers to let you submit the return yourself and hands it over, you submit it with exactly the details the agent gives you, and you read back the RMA number it gives you. When you have an RMA number for the bearings, you thank the agent, say you will have the crib pack them up, and end the call.
